footnotes: From pre-tax loss to net loss to Viper Energy: includes a $19.0M income tax benefit, $138M of losses allocated to noncontrolling interests; after $1.0M of preferred dividends. The filing reports no separate capital expenditures, so free cash flow equals operating cash flow.

Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC (income statement lines as the filing presents them); free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue rose 62.0% to $1.4B in 2025. The company had an operating loss of $140M, versus operating income of $567M.

The company had a net loss of $69.0M, or −$0.48 per share, versus net income of $359M. Operating cash flow was $1.1B and free cash flow $1.1B, versus $620M; Viper Energy returned $328M through dividends.
sources: Viper Energy, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)
